name: jupp
why: A Joe-derived console editor with an old-school lineage, a close call for a rarely seen editor.

brief.what_it_is: A console text editor described in its Homebrew formula as a professional screen editor for programmers. The formula installs seven executables: jupp, joe, jmacs, jpico, jstar, rjoe, and termidx. The scout notes describe it as Joe-derived, but I could not verify that because the homepage did not load. Input is text files opened in a terminal, and output is the edited files. Nothing beyond the formula metadata and scout notes was confirmed.
brief.why_it_exists: Not confirmed. The homepage that would state the author's framing was unreachable, so I cannot give the project's own reason for existing.
brief.install_notes: Installed with brew install jupp. The Homebrew formula gives no extra configuration, accounts, runtimes, or first-run steps, and I could not read the project documentation to check for any.
brief.standout: Unverified. The executable names suggest the project ships several editor personalities in one package: jmacs and jpico look like Emacs- and Pico-style front ends, and rjoe may be a restricted or remote variant of joe. These are inferences from the names alone. The scout notes call it a rarely seen editor with an old-school lineage.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage failed to load, so I found no release date, commit history, or maintenance note.
brief.caveats: The homepage https://mbsd.evolvis.org/jupp.htm was unreachable (URLError), so the description, lineage, and feature claims rest only on the Homebrew formula metadata and the scout notes. The Homebrew caveats field is empty. No README, docs, or demo were available to read.
